title: Armes v. Southwest Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery erred in ruling Armes’s complaint out of order and denying him a hearing, and remanded the case to Presbytery.
first_summary: After Armes was excommunicated, Presbytery refused to hear his complaint, first reasoning that excommunication deprived him of standing and later ruling the complaint untimely. Presbytery conceded that it had erred, and the parties stipulated to remand. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded it to Presbytery for a hearing.
summary: Presbytery refused to hear Armes’s complaint against his excommunication, initially reasoning that excommunication deprived him of standing and later ruling the complaint untimely. Presbytery conceded its error on the standing ground, and all parties stipulated to remand for a hearing. The SJC confirmed that stipulation, sustained the complaint, and remanded the case without deciding the validity of the excommunication itself.
